title: Real Madrid Launch Operation to Sign Rodri From Manchester City
excerpt: The Spanish giants have reversed their summer stance on the World Cup Golden Ball winner, with talks underway over a contract through 2030 as José Mourinho pushes for the deal.
body:
• Real Madrid have performed a dramatic U-turn and are now actively working to sign Manchester City midfielder Rodri before the transfer window closes.
  • Representatives from Real Madrid held a secret meeting with Rodri's agents in Pozuelo, Madrid, offering a contract until 2030.
  • Head coach José Mourinho has personally urged club president Florentino Pérez to complete the transfer after Rodri's World Cup-winning performances.
  • Manchester City deny any formal contact but are prepared to listen to offers around €60 million, with Rodri entering the final year of his contract.

Real Madrid are now fully committed to signing Manchester City midfielder Rodri this summer, according to multiple reports, marking a stunning reversal of the Spanish club's transfer strategy following the 30-year-old's dominant performances at the 2026 World Cup.

According to David Ornstein of The Athletic and Patrick Berger of Sky Sports Germany, Madrid have moved from internal discussions to concrete negotiations, with the club operating under the assumption that the Spain international will join before the window closes.

From Denial to Determination

The shift has been swift and dramatic. Throughout the early months of the summer, sources at the Bernabéu repeatedly insisted Rodri was not part of their recruitment plans. The club had focused on other targets, including Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez, only to be priced out of that deal.

https://x.com/433/status/2080722088701178284

Everything changed after Spain's World Cup triumph in North America. Rodri captained Luis de la Fuente's side through all eight matches, anchoring the midfield as Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the final to claim their second World Cup title. He was awarded the Golden Ball as the tournament's outstanding player — a recognition that added to his 2024 Ballon d'Or crown.

"What seemed impossible a few weeks ago is now possible."

— ESPN, reporting on internal sentiment at Real Madrid

Those performances convinced key figures inside Real Madrid that Rodri remains the ideal anchor for their midfield rebuild. General manager José Ángel Sánchez and head scout Juni Calafat are reportedly leading the push to get the deal done.

Secret Meeting in Pozuelo

The operation has already moved beyond theoretical interest. Earlier this week, Real Madrid emissaries held a private meeting with Rodri's agents in Pozuelo, an affluent suburb of Madrid. During those discussions, the club outlined a long-term project featuring a four-year contract through June 2030.

Rodri, a Madrid native who began his professional career at Atlético Madrid before joining City in 2019, made clear he would welcome the opportunity to return to Spanish football. He has never hidden that desire.

"Would I like to play in Spain again, in La Liga, in Madrid? I would like to return, yes, obviously. Having played for Atlético before would not prevent me from playing for Real Madrid. You can't turn down one of the world's best clubs."

— Rodri, speaking during the March international break

The Mourinho Factor

Behind the scenes, head coach José Mourinho has been instrumental in accelerating the pursuit. According to journalist Roberto Gómez on Radio MARCA, Mourinho has made an explicit request to club president Florentino Pérez: he wants Rodri at all costs.

The Portuguese manager sees the midfielder as the specialist Real Madrid have lacked since Toni Kroos retired — a player capable of controlling tempo, winning the ball in transition, and providing the platform for more creative players like Jude Bellingham to operate freely.

Pérez had initially resisted due to concerns about Rodri's age and injury history. The midfielder is approaching his 31st birthday and battled back from a serious ACL injury that disrupted much of his 2024-25 season. He now faces surgery on a back problem sustained during the World Cup, with no definitive timeline for his return.

Despite those risks, the latest reports indicate Pérez has softened his position. The club is prepared to proceed regardless of the surgery timeline.

Manchester City's Position

Manchester City have publicly denied any contact from Real Madrid, with sources from within the club claiming the speculation stems solely from Rodri's World Cup exploits. New manager Enzo Maresca appeared unfazed by the uncertainty at his Friday unveiling.

City continue to hold talks with Rodri over a contract extension, but no agreement has been reached. With his deal expiring in June 2027, the club faces a familiar dilemma: accept a fee now or risk losing a prized asset for free next year. Reports from Diario AS indicate City would be prepared to listen to offers around €60 million.

To fund the move, Real Madrid have signaled a willingness to sell Aurélien Tchouaméni, who has attracted interest from Manchester United at a valuation of approximately €80 million.

What Comes Next

Formal club-to-club negotiations have not yet begun, which remains the most significant hurdle. Real Madrid must bridge the gap between their growing internal confidence and the practical reality of dealing with a Manchester City side that has no obligation to sell.

The transfer window's closing deadline adds urgency. Real Madrid appear prepared to act quickly — but whether Manchester City cooperate, or Rodri's back surgery complicates the timeline further, will determine whether one of the summer's most dramatic transfer sagas reaches its expected conclusion.
